summary: Adds migration system/0003 that catches up with an earlier model edit (Role.depts M2M gets related_name='roles'); this is a Django state-only change with no SQL/table change; also commits an updated dev db.sqlite3.

statements.text: Nothing flagged (plain reads logins, payments, database changes and secrets. It doesn't run the code, and it can miss bugs.)
statements.why: No code, endpoint or permission changes; the migration only alters related_name/verbose_name and emits no SQL.
True, but doesn't say it's the checked-in dev database (settings_dev.py) that must not be copied over a live database.

statements.text: 1. Apply server/apps/system/migrations/0003_auto_20220227_1732.py too (`python manage.py migrate`). It only records settings Django keeps in your code (like labels, or the name for related records), not changes to your tables, so nothing breaks if it runs later.
statements.why: Migration 0003 is a single AlterField on Role.depts setting related_name='roles' and verbose_name; a ManyToMany related_name change emits no SQL, so running it later is harmless. Accurate and correctly low-stakes.

misses.what: The commit also updates the checked-in dev SQLite database (server/db.sqlite3, used by settings_dev.py); it carries whatever dev data/accounts are in it and is not something to deploy over a live database. The card lists the file but doesn't say what it is.
